main_text.p: furditatem suæ produnt opinionis, tum quòd animo se designare sedem opinantes nullam designant, tum quòd puncta à corporum communione, quanquàm ex illis omnia constent corpora, excludere coguntur metuentes ne puncta corporibus accensendo dimensionem animi sedes habeat; Discant nullas inter corpus & spiritum medias dari substantias.
main_text.head: I.
Ornatissimo atq; Doctissimo Dn. Defendenti.

p.i: Dulcia non meruit, qui non gustavit amara: Sic Tibi sudanti jam dulcia præmia confert Musa; Dies noctesq; sonant, en! digna merenti! Junxisti studiis animum, quem æquabit Olympo Laude Minerva.

main_text.p: Indissolubilis amicitiæ tesseram, scripsit Musâ & Apolline nullo, Joh. Casp. Seelmatter.
main_text.head: II.
Acclamatio Annagrammatico echica CORNELIUS HENTZIUS. Ἀναγραμματισμὸς. VIRTUS ZELO HISCENS.
main_text.p: ECho responde dulces quem quæro Camenæ? Mene rogas? Respondebis qua Mente? Libente; Nonne sacri Suadæ Tripodes hunc Edocuere? Vere; Virtutis raræ num Zelj glíscit Amore? More; sed hinc quæso dic quanta feret Bona? Dona. Multane dona Feret? Meret; en in nomine Zelum? Coelum? Nam novit cœli perrumpere Fores. O Res! Vox resonans nunc plura Tacebo; Valebo.

p.i: In symbolum æternum duraturæ fraternitatis appositi

page.notes: Ornamental rules and the Greek anagram line are reproduced as best legible; the Greek line is transcribed as read. Some letters in the Latin acclamation are uncertain due to print wear. The verse lines have been set as one paragraph where the printed lines were run together, and the initial D and E are large drop capitals.
